title: Science, art and shared wonder

budget.purpose: Banksia Hall and Paperbark Quiet Room venue booking, including setup/pack-down window and seating/wayfinding access
Version-1 covered courtyard add-on for an art/observation activity
Two art/observation pack-sets, covering potential participation by 80 people at 40 people per set
Quiet-room sensory support kit for up to 20 people at a time
Non-alcoholic drinks and labeled simple snacks for up to 80 adults

programme.title: Setup: room, quiet-space and wayfinding set-out; chair count and access-route check
Welcome, plain-language framing and access/wayfinding orientation
Short science talks and conversation: two speakers, familiar examples, no audience experiments
Guided room change and chair transfer: 40 people and chairs move from Hall to Courtyard
Guided room change and chair transfer: Courtyard arrival
Art and observation workshop: look, sketch and compare; reusable viewing cards
Guided room change and chair transfer: 20 people and chairs move from Courtyard to Hall
Guided room change and chair transfer: Hall arrival
Light refreshments and informal conversation, with service staged for the Hall and Courtyard
Pack-down, chair inventory and clear-room check

risks.issue: Room transitions, attendance distribution and movement of 40 chairs may create congestion or obstruct step-free routes. The v1 plan places up to 80 people across Hall/Quiet (60/20) and then Hall/Courtyard/Quiet (20/40/20), with chair transfers during two 15-minute transitions. The fictional rooms have capacities of 80, 20 and 40 respectively; the route, floor plan and handling time are unverified.
risks.mitigation: Proposed, not implemented: confirm a scaled floor plan and step-free routes; assign named people separately to crowd direction and furniture handling; count attendees before and after each move; keep exits and aisles clear; do not exceed room or total capacity. If the 40-chair transfer cannot be completed safely within the window, use the creative team's Hall rotation alternative and revise the schedule and staffing before integration.

risks.issue: Step-free room descriptions and a sign set do not establish that the final layout, route, seating distribution or signs work for attendees. The two stewards also have competing wayfinding, occupancy-counting and chair-moving tasks during transitions.
risks.owner: Event lead / access lead (to be appointed by the human owner)
risks.mitigation: Proposed, not implemented: inspect the fictional floor plan with access needs in mind; confirm clear routes, sightlines, sign placement, seating and a route between rooms; test the arrangement and transition before the event; assign a dedicated transition lead and avoid asking stewards to move furniture while directing attendees.

risks.issue: The volunteer plan assumes 14 donated volunteer-hours, but availability is not confirmed. The quiet-room host is assigned 18:30–20:30 while quiet-space use begins at 18:20; the public programme continues to 20:45. A staffing gap could leave transitions, wayfinding or the quiet option unsupported.
risks.mitigation: Proposed, not implemented: confirm each role and exact coverage window; identify a backup for the lead and stewards; either extend quiet-room host coverage through the public window or clearly schedule and staff a quiet-space closure at 20:30. Do not treat the in-kind card as an availability commitment.

risks.issue: The source card says snacks are labeled, but ingredients, allergen labeling, cross-contact controls, service layout and attendee dietary needs are not established. Hall and Courtyard service for 60 attendees may also create queues in circulation areas.
risks.mitigation: Proposed, not implemented: obtain and check ingredient and allergen information with the service provider; decide how food is separated and served; keep queues and food away from exits and step-free routes; offer a clear route for questions without collecting attendee personal data for this exercise. If adequate information or service arrangements cannot be confirmed, revise or omit the affected food items in a human-approved plan.

risks.issue: The exercise prohibits attendee personal data. A later attempt to manage access or dietary needs by collecting identifiable information would exceed this fictional plan's scope and create unnecessary privacy exposure.
risks.mitigation: Proposed, not implemented: keep this rehearsal free of attendee data collection. Any real-world access or dietary planning process requires a separate human decision defining purpose, minimum necessary data, handling and retention before collection; this output grants no such authority.

Join a welcoming evening for 80 adults, titled “Science, art and shared wonder,” to explore familiar science ideas through short talks, an art-and-observation workshop, and informal conversation over light refreshments. A quiet-space option is planned alongside the main programme. The draft schedule is 18:00–21:00 Perth local time on 14 November 2026, at the fictional Banksia Hall venue. Room access, staffing, transitions, and refreshment arrangements remain subject to human review; no venue, service, or accessibility details are confirmed.
